report_type: CRYPTO SPOT PRICE-SIGNAL RESEARCH for LINK-USD. Long-only. Paper only.

assumptions.target_fill: requires trade-through by the slippage buffer

chart_exits.question: At the same dollar risk per trade, do stops and targets taken from support/resistance zones earn more than fixed ATR exits on the same entries?
chart_exits.verdict_reason: only 64 paired out-of-sample trades; at least 100 are needed
notes: Compared on identical entries; R is measured against each method's own stop, so both risk the same dollars per trade.
Trades with no clean chart plan are passed by the chart method; see the skip counts and the 'skips as zero' totals.
Chart zones at each entry use only candles that had closed by then.

trend_pullback.label: trend_pullback@1.0#1458e1ec

spec.name: trend_pullback
spec.hypothesis: When the 1-hour and 4-hour trends are up, a shallow dip to the 21-bar average that is bought back tends to continue up.
spec.why_crypto: Crypto trends persist for hours to days, and dips in a trend are bought quickly because the market never closes.
spec.trigger: close of the candle above the prior candle's high after touching the 21-bar average, with the 1h and 4h trend up and Bitcoin not falling.
spec.targets: Half at 1.5R, half at 3R (stop to entry after the first).

donchian_breakout.label: donchian_breakout@1.0#2c43d62c

spec.name: donchian_breakout
spec.hypothesis: A strong close above the highest price of the last 24 hours, on heavy volume, tends to keep running.
spec.why_crypto: Crypto momentum is persistent, and with no market close, breakouts are not erased by an overnight gap-and-fade.
spec.trigger: First candle close above the prior 24-hour high, closing in the top 30% of its range, with volume at least 1.5x normal.
spec.stop_logic: 2 x ATR below entry (breakouts need room).

squeeze_breakout.label: squeeze_breakout@1.0#85bf601a

spec.name: squeeze_breakout
spec.hypothesis: After an unusually quiet stretch, price often breaks out fast. Buy the first strong close above the upper band.
spec.why_crypto: Crypto volatility comes in clusters: long quiet squeezes are followed by sharp moves.
spec.trigger: Price range in the quietest fifth of the last week for most of the last hour (or last four candles), then a close above the upper Bollinger band on above-normal volume.

oversold_bounce.label: oversold_bounce@1.0#612af972

spec.name: oversold_bounce
spec.hypothesis: A sudden flush far below the normal range snaps back once price turns up (forced sellers are done).
spec.why_crypto: Leveraged liquidations create fast wicks well outside the normal range that often retrace within hours.
spec.trigger: A bar pierced the lower 2.5-sigma band with RSI under 30 in the last 3 bars, then a close above the prior high and above its own open. Not taken in a 4-hour downtrend.
spec.targets: Half at 1R, half at 2R (mean reversion takes quicker profits).

range_bounce.label: range_bounce@1.0#6ed88bd5

spec.name: range_bounce
spec.hypothesis: In a sideways market, a dip under the lower band that closes back inside tends to return to the middle.
spec.why_crypto: Crypto spends long stretches in ranges between big moves; weekends in particular can be quiet and range-bound.
spec.trigger: 1-hour ADX under 20, a dip under the lower Bollinger band, a close back above it, RSI under 40, and a green candle.

btc_lead.label: btc_lead@1.0#314a476d

spec.name: btc_lead
spec.hypothesis: When Bitcoin makes a big move up and the coin has barely moved yet, the coin tends to catch up.
spec.why_crypto: Bitcoin leads the rest of the crypto market; smaller coins often follow with a delay.
spec.trigger: Bitcoin's last-hour gain is at least 1.5x its typical hour while this coin gained under 40% of that, on a green candle.

support_bounce.label: support_bounce@1.0#47b0400e

spec.name: support_bounce
spec.hypothesis: In an uptrend (higher highs and higher lows), price that dips back to the last higher low and is rejected tends to resume up.
spec.why_crypto: Classic chart support. Crypto trends persist and dips to prior swing lows are widely watched, so reactions there are common.
spec.trigger: Uptrend structure on the entry chart and the 1h chart; a candle dips to within a quarter ATR of the last swing low (never more than one ATR below it) and closes back above it in the top part of its range.

swing_breakout.label: swing_breakout@1.0#c070786d

spec.name: swing_breakout
spec.hypothesis: A strong close above the last confirmed swing high, on above-normal volume, in an uptrend, tends to continue.
spec.why_crypto: Classic breakout above resistance. Stops resting above swing highs add fuel when they are taken out.
spec.trigger: First candle close above the last confirmed swing high, in the top 30% of its range, volume at least 1.3x normal, and the entry-chart structure is not a downtrend.

zone_rejection.label: zone_rejection@1.0#27348c24

spec.name: zone_rejection
spec.hypothesis: A candle that dips into a strong support zone and is rejected, while the bigger trend is up and there is room to run, tends to bounce.
spec.why_crypto: How chart traders actually use support: only strong zones, only with the bigger trend, only with a rejection candle, stop behind the zone.
spec.trigger: Bullish rejection candle (closes in the top 40% of its range, lower wick at least 40% of range, range at least 0.8 ATR) while the 1-hour trend is up; then the chart checklist must pass: bigger trend up, strong support zone touched, entry within 1.5 ATR of it.
spec.targets: Just under the next resistance zones; at least 2R of room is required.

multiple_testing.note: Bonferroni-adjusted across all 120 strategy-by-coin tests, so adding coins makes the pass bar stricter. No parameter search was run, so nothing was tuned on the data.

limitations: Bootstrap CIs ignore serial correlation between trades.
AERO trades mainly on the Aerodrome DEX on Base; this uses the Coinbase AERO-USD price as a stand-in, so real DEX costs and slippage can differ.
Slippage per coin is an assumption (smaller or thinner coins get a larger number). Real fills can be worse, especially in fast markets.
Only one market regime may be covered; crypto cycles are long.
Past results do not predict future results.
